carlos: Heads-up — after the kernel selector change rolled in yesterday I see a small but consistent p95 latency increase on a subset of endpoints. digging in now, but initial signal points to lower prompt-cache hit-rate when continuous batching mixes shorter and longer prefixes.

maya: Ack. which kernel change specifically? the heuristic that prefers fused-kernel for seq_len<=128?

carlos: Yeah that one (v3.1.4). benchmark shows fused kernel reduces per-token compute but it changes scheduling slightly; batch composition is drifting so cached prefixes aren't reused as often.

bench-bot: perf/summary job #8421 finished:
```
hit_rate_before: 0.71
hit_rate_after: 0.58
p50_latency_before: 22ms
p50_latency_after: 24ms
p95_latency_before: 47ms
p95_latency_after: 53ms
throughput_delta: -3%
```

olga: Oof. So continuous batching is mixing cohorts and evicting KV entries sooner? or keying changed?

carlos: Two interacting factors: (1) kernel change changes micro-batching timing which increases inter-arrival variance -> batcher composes more mixed-length batches. (2) our cache key currently uses raw prompt hash + model+ver, but not cohort-aware TTLs, so mixed batches reduce prefix reuse.

maya: Can we reproduce locally with the workload replay? I can spin up a small rig to emulate request distribution.

ryan: I think we should try a quick change: make cache "polite" to continuous batching by adding a small sticky window (cohort_id derived from client route + recent sequence-length bucket). That way evictions for one cohort don't punish another.

olga: Also consider adjusting batcher threshold: if we bias to wait up to 6ms for more similar seq_len joins, hit-rate might improve at slight latency cost. worth A/Bing.

bench-bot: replay job #8422 queued (traffic-sim: mixed-50/50 short/long).

carlos: Plan: 1) reproduce with replay, 2) run A/B: (A) kernel v3.1.4 + current cache, (B) kernel v3.1.4 + polite-cache+cohort-ttl, (C) kernel v3.0.9 baseline. measure hit-rate, p95, tokens/sec.

maya: I'll own running the replay and attach profiles. can we capture kernel selection traces + batch composition histograms?

olga: Add KV cache hit-heatmaps too (per-cohort). put results in the perf dashboard.

ryan: Minimal patch for polite-cache: patch cache key -> "prompt_hash|model|cohort_bucket" and add sliding-window TTL 10s (config flag). will draft PR.

carlos: If A/B shows hit_rate recovery w/o losing throughput -> we can roll patch behind feature-flag. if not, consider reverting kernel selection or tweak batcher timing.

maya: Replay started. I'll post logs & flamegraphs here when done.

bench-bot: replay job #8422 started at 2026-03-18T15:04:02Z

carlos: Thanks. filing a short triage ticket: INF-2107 capturing regression, linking kernel PR and batcher traces. assign to eng-runtime.

olga: +1. also adding observability alert: if hit_rate drops >8% within 30m trigger automated rollback candidate list.

ryan: PR draft incoming in a bit. trying to keep the change small and toggleable.

maya: Results: replay shows polite-cache recovers hit_rate to ~0.69 and p95 back within 1-2ms of baseline. attaching flamegraph gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/perf/xyz123

carlos: Nice. let's run a 2h canary behind flag then schedule a gradual rollout. great catch all. :thumbsup:
